title: Don't Believe Everything You Think
alternate_titles: Don't Believe Everything You Think: Why Your Thinking Is The Beginning & End Of Suffering

editions.label: Expanded edition
editions.publisher: Authors Equity / Books By Joseph Nguyen

contents: The root cause of suffering: not events and not thoughts, but thinking
Thoughts versus thinking: spontaneous mental events versus the elaboration we add
The inside-out claim: feelings come from thought, not circumstances
Non-thinking, flow, and intuition: the mind that quiets hears its own wisdom
Goals from inspiration versus goals from desperation
Unconditional love and peace as the default state beneath thinking
Chapter summaries and reflection questions throughout; short chapters, deliberately repetitive

audiences: Overthinkers meeting thought-distancing ideas for the first time
Readers who want spiritual self-help without jargon or length
People in low-stakes distress; not a substitute for clinical care

sources.title: Don't Believe Everything You Think (Expanded Edition)
sources.supports: Expanded edition bibliographic facts: ISBN 9798893310153 under the Books By Joseph Nguyen imprint, and the publisher description of the thesis.

sources.title: Don't Believe Everything You Think
sources.supports: Publication date 2022-03-28, ~175 pages, 3.79 average over ~68,000 ratings, and the documented split: praised as a lifeline for overthinkers; criticised as repetitive, evidence-free, oversimplified, and spiritually unattributed.
sources.limitations: Self-selected raters; used for both content structure and reception.

sources.title: Review of Don't Believe Everything You Think (Authors Equity, 2024)
sources.supports: A therapist's substantive critique: the thought/thinking dichotomy misdescribes experience (first reactions arrive loaded — the Stoics' 'impression', REBT's 'activating event'); letting go of thoughts 'is simple in the way that running a marathon is simple' and the training is omitted; verdict 'radically incomplete but potentially misleading' despite elegant presentation; notes the PAUSE method as the useful part and the Authors Equity 2024 edition.
sources.limitations: Personal Substack of a practising therapist and philosophy PhD; single reviewer.

sources.title: Don't Believe Everything You Think by Joseph Nguyen (review essay)
sources.supports: An analysis mapping the book onto Acceptance and Commitment Therapy: its moves are cognitive defusion and acceptance simplified for lay readers, effective as a gateway, without ACT's methodological rigour or evidence base.
sources.limitations: Personal Medium essay; credentials as stated by the author.

sources.title: The Best Books Come from the Greatest Pains: Joseph Nguyen
sources.supports: Origin story (written out of the author's own overthinking and self-doubt), the Zen-inspired framing, the self-published-to-Authors-Equity path, 2M+ copies in 30+ languages, and the forthcoming follow-up.

sources.title: Joseph Nguyen — Don't Believe Everything You Think
sources.supports: The author's own framing: NYT and international bestseller status, 31+ languages, and the book's promise of discovering the root cause of suffering.

sources.title: Three Principles Psychology
sources.supports: Context for the unattributed tradition the book's inside-out claims parallel: the Mind/Consciousness/Thought framework from Sydney Banks, its limited evidence base, and documented criticisms including the charge of belief-system-as-science.
sources.limitations: Documents the tradition, not the book; the parallel is noted by critical reviewers, not acknowledged by the author.

workflow.coverage_notes: Built from the publisher record, two independent professional reviews (one substantively critical), a documented interview, the reader-reception record, and context on the unattributed tradition; no full-text read.
